chunks: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated to us, from Usayd ibn Thaʿlabah, from Umm Hāniʾ.
She said: I met Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام), and I asked him about this verse.
“But nay! I swear by the retreating ones, the runners, the concealers.”

He said: “The retreating one is an Imam who goes into concealment in his time, when his knowledge is cut off from the people, in the year two hundred and sixty. Then he will appear like a blazing meteor in the darkness of the night.”
“So if you live to see that, your eye will be gladdened.”

key_terms.إِمَامٌ: the divinely appointed leader referred to in this narration
key_terms.الْخُنَّسُ: the concealed or retreating one, interpreted here as the hidden Imam
key_terms.انْقِطَاعٍ: a cutting off or interruption, here of access to his knowledge
key_terms.سَنَةَ سِتِّينَ وَمِائَتَيْنِ: the year two hundred and sixty, given here as the time marker for the concealment
key_terms.عِلْمِهِ: his knowledge, meaning the Imam’s accessible guidance among the people
key_terms.قَرَّتْ عَيْنُكِ: your eye will be gladdened, meaning you will be delighted and comforted
key_terms.كَالشِّهَابِ الْوَاقِدِ: like a blazing meteor, describing the forceful clarity of his appearance
key_terms.يَخْنِسُ: goes into concealment or withdraws from public view

ai.seo_question: How is the verse about الْخُنَّسِ interpreted in Shia hadith as referring to the Imam’s ghaybah (occultation)?
ai.summary: This narration presents the verse as referring to an Imam who enters ghaybah (occultation), becoming hidden from the people at a time when access to his knowledge is cut off. It describes a later reappearance with striking imagery, likening it to a blazing meteor in the darkness of night, and connects the verse to the doctrine of the hidden Imam.
